title: Towards Lean 4 Formalization of the Free Energy Principle: AI-Driven Theorem Sketching and Verification for Active Inference and Bayesian Mechanics
description:
FEP_Lean / FEP Formal v1.6.0 is a reproducible catalogue of 168 canonical Lean topic bodies in 22 reviewed families across the Free Energy Principle, Active Inference, Bayesian Mechanics, Information Geometry and Thermodynamics. Each topic retains its carrier, exact qualified statement, assumptions, non-vacuity boundary, semantic disposition and evidence requirements. Lean and Mathlib are pinned to 4.34.1.

This version adds a greatly extended Supplement A, modular installed-package mathematical methods, source-grounded Lean statement and natural-language analysis, and reproducible publication figures and an offline explorer. It compares 22 FEP family context unions with twelve selected OpenAI mathematics result units in 30 explicitly authored binary coordinates. The deterministic MDS projection reports its spectrum, distance distortion, stress and axis ambiguity. The upstream corpus is pinned at adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a; its statements are reference comparisons, with no imported proof authority or runtime dependency.

Compilation establishes the exact selected Lean bodies, not the Free Energy Principle as a physical theory. Semantic maturity is separate from compilation. Numerical and embedding visualizations are explanatory evidence. Frozen H3 primary execution, full seven-stage capture, Q7 generated-runner execution, provider runs and future empirical work retain their separate acceptance requirements.

The release includes the manuscript PDF, offline companion, Python wheel and source distribution, exact tagged repository source and SHA-256 checksums. Source: ActiveInferenceInstitute/fep_formal. Release: v1.6.0. This manuscript continues scholarly concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19699233; GitHub software archives are maintained separately under concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23196891.

methods.name: Curated catalog of 50 FEP topics as namespaced Lean 4 sketches against Mathlib4
methods.description: Compiled 50 topics across five pillars (FEP, Active Inference, Bayesian Mechanics, Information Geometry, Thermodynamics) as Lean 4 sketches from a single source of truth.
methods.evidence: We address this gap with a curated catalog of 50 topics that spans the five technical pillars of the framework

methods.name: Native lake env lean verification on a pinned Lean/Mathlib v4.29.0 stack
methods.description: Verified every reported compilation result with a real lake env lean invocation against the pinned toolchain, with no mocked compilers or synthetic success signals.
methods.evidence: Every reported compilation result is produced by a real lake env lean invocation against the pinned Lean 4 4.29.0 toolchain and Mathlib4 v4.29.0.

methods.name: LLM-assisted commentary pipeline (Hermes/OpenGauss, kimi-k2.6 via OpenRouter)
methods.description: Layered LLM drafting and commentary over the catalog, cached by Lean source hash, with the Lean kernel kept as sole ground truth for compilation claims.
methods.evidence: the language model can draft, explain, and cross-link each sketch, while the Lean 4 kernel remains sole ground truth for every compilation claim in the manuscript.

methods.name: Zero-mock test suite with coverage gate and SQLite run persistence
methods.description: Ran 347 tests that each exercise real files, a real SQLite store, live compiler calls or actual HTTP calls, holding coverage above an 89% CI gate.
methods.evidence: every one of the 347 test cases exercises a real file, a real SQLite store, a live compiler invocation, or an actual HTTP call

methods.name: Three-level sorry-aware maturity taxonomy (real / partial / aspirational)
methods.description: Introduced a classification intended to make incomplete formalization explicit; all current rows are tagged real.
methods.evidence: We introduce a three-level sorry-aware classification (real / partial / aspirational) that makes incomplete formalization honest and auditable.

key_findings: On the pinned Lean 4 / Mathlib4 v4.29.0 stack, the shipped catalog compiles 50/50 sorry-free.
The Hermes-assisted Gauss run run_20260424_064334 achieved 50/50 clean compiles with 0 sorry and 0 errors.
Constructions that already typecheck in today's Mathlib4 include finite-set probability, Bayesian updating, finite-space KL divergence and variational free-energy bounds.
The author cautions that the catalog covers definitional lemmas and structural identities rather than end-to-end FEP theorems, and many rows stop short of what the informal text proves.
Formal verification here establishes formal adequacy only; it provides no empirical confirmation that brains minimize variational free energy.
key_findings_evidence: On the pinned stack leanprover/lean4:v4.29.0 / Mathlib4 v4.29.0 the shipped catalog compiles 50/50 sorry-free under lake env lean
Hermes-assisted Gauss run run_20260424_064334 (~2 min) achieved 50/50 clean compiles, 0 sorry, 0 errors

an initial set of FEP-related constructions that already typecheck against today’s Mathlib4 — finite-set probability, Bayesian updating, Kullback–Leibler divergence on finite spaces, variational free-energy bounds

The current catalogue covers definitional lemmas and structural identities (type disci- pline, algebraic identities, measure-monotonicity, skew-symmetry) rather than end-to-end theorems of the FEP dynamical program.
A formally verified theorem about variational free energy says nothing about whether biological brains minimize variational free energy.
